newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee body favours retail price hikes.
newsitem.headline: German coffee body favours retail price hikes.

text.p: German coffee industry association DKV said sharply higher futures prices, firm differentials and a strong dollar were inflating roasters' costs and made further retail price rises look inevitable.
"Price rises are more than necessary from an operational point of view," a DKV spokesman said on Friday in response to an enquiry.
"The intention is there, but it remains to be seen how this can be implemented."
Roasters had told the DKV they would have liked to have added three marks per 500 grams to the average price of roasted coffee, which stood seven marks in January 1997.
But at the end of April, average retail prices were just above 7.50 marks, DKV figures showed.
Analysts estimated some 0.10-0.20 marks were added to retail prices in May.

Market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) on Monday said it was unhappy with the net effect of two price rises in Germany earlier this year and that a further 1.50-2.00 marks would probably need to be added to KJS products in June.
KJS is part of Philip Morris.
Second largest roaster Tchibo on Friday said it would leave its prices unchanged after May 2 increases of 0.50-1.00 marks.
A spokeswoman for Hamburg-based roaster J.J. Darboven said further price increases could be justified but no firm decisions had yet been taken.
New York arabica futures on Thursday hit 20-year highs in some contracts amid fund buying and against a background of tight fundamental supplies.
German coffee blends include around 70 percent of so-called washed arabicas, expensive varieties whose prices attract hefty premiums over unwashed grades and robusta coffees.
Roasters maintain they will not compromise on quality -- although Brazils and robustas are more readily available.
"Roasters will have to keep up the quality of their products...otherwise consumers would notice the difference and could turn to other drinks," the DKV spokesman said.
However, Vietnam robustas more than doubled their share of German January net imports to 89,689 bags (41,936 in December), making the country the third largest supplier.
Vietnam in 1996 held 11th place among suppliers.
